sources.text: A newsletter says, 'Aria hates meetings.' I am forwarding the quote, not asserting it.

values.value-quote: The newsletter claims Aria hates meetings; it is not Aria's preference.

reason: The quoted speaker is an outside source. The quote supplies no direct host preference.

sources.text: Last winter I wanted to accept every new meeting request.
I changed my mind. This year I want fewer meetings and longer focus blocks.

values.value-new-preference: Current preference for fewer meetings and longer focus blocks.

reason: The later direct statement revises a preference; the earlier position must remain historically visible.

sources.text: Calendar: presentation planned for April 14. Attendance not confirmed.

reason: A calendar plan does not prove the scheduled event occurred.

sources.text: I attest that Mira played the violin as a child. This is about Mira, not me.

values.value-mira-violin: Mira played violin as a child.
values.value-ben-violin: Ben played violin as a child.

reason: The owner attests a separate source person's history; this is not a host autobiography.

sources.text: Generated rehearsal: Perhaps Mira would have declined this job. This was invented for practice.

values.value-rehearsal: A possible fictional response was rehearsed.

reason: Generated rehearsal can teach a conditional pattern but is not historical evidence.

sources.text: Delete my old travel log and anything derived from it. I no longer authorize its use.

values.value-delete: Request to delete the old travel log and its derivatives.
values.value-deleted: The old travel log has already been erased everywhere.

reason: A request is not proof that deletion or derivative rebuilding has completed.

sources.text: We chose the prototype despite a risk of missing the paper deadline.
Prototype succeeded. Paper deadline was missed. Both happened.

values.value-mixed: Prototype succeeded and the paper deadline was missed.
values.value-only-success: The choice was an unqualified success.

reason: Preserve both gains and costs and link the outcome to its earlier choice.

sources.text: Across three projects, Cy starts another task when anxious about the current one.
When you see that pattern, ask me before adding a new project. Show the evidence each time.

values.value-norm: Ask with evidence before starting a new project when the pattern recurs.
values.value-permanent: Cy must refuse every new project permanently.

reason: The owner negotiated a contextual interaction norm, not a permanent identity or blanket refusal.

sources.text: Assistant log: I gave a confident answer and later found I had missed a source. I should flag this failure mode.

values.value-calibration: Assistant observed its own overconfidence after a missed source.
values.value-source-past: A separate source person made this mistake in childhood.

reason: An assistant's post-activation failure belongs to its developing self, not a source person's past.

sources.text: Practice scenario: imagine Cy sold the lab. No sale took place.

values.value-practice: A fictional sale was rehearsed as a scenario.
values.value-sale: Cy sold the lab in real life.

reason: A hypothetical event can train conditional behavior but cannot become lived host history.

sources.text: The assistant observed the same import, clean, verify, summarize sequence on several weeks; the last run missed an edge case.

values.value-skill: Candidate repeated workflow requires testing before skill promotion.
values.value-perfect: The workflow is already reliable and should be promoted.

reason: Repeated action suggests a candidate skill. The observed edge-case failure prevents promotion as reliable procedure.
